nodes.name: Archaeological Theory
nodes.description: The theoretical frameworks guiding how archaeologists interpret the material past.

nodes.name: Archaeological Method
nodes.description: The field and laboratory techniques used to recover and analyze the material record.

nodes.name: Prehistoric Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of societies without written records.

nodes.name: Historical Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of periods with written records, combining texts and material evidence.

nodes.name: Classical Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of the Greek and Roman worlds.

nodes.name: Egyptology
nodes.description: The study of ancient Egypt, its language, archaeology, and culture.

nodes.name: Near Eastern Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of Mesopotamia and the ancient Near East.

nodes.name: Underwater Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of submerged sites and shipwrecks.

nodes.name: Bioarchaeology
nodes.description: The study of human remains to reconstruct past lives, health, and diet.

nodes.name: Zooarchaeology
nodes.description: The study of animal remains from archaeological sites.

nodes.name: Archaeobotany
nodes.description: The study of plant remains from archaeological sites.

nodes.name: Geoarchaeology
nodes.description: The application of earth-science methods to archaeological questions.

nodes.name: Landscape Archaeology
nodes.description: The study of how past peoples shaped and inhabited their landscapes.

nodes.name: Ethnoarchaeology
nodes.description: The use of living societies to model how archaeological sites formed.

nodes.name: Experimental Archaeology
nodes.description: The reconstruction and testing of past technologies and practices.

nodes.name: Computational Archaeology
nodes.description: The use of computation, GIS, and modeling in archaeological research.

nodes.name: Environmental Archaeology
nodes.description: The study of past human-environment interactions through material remains.

nodes.name: Industrial Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of industry, machines, and industrial landscapes.

nodes.name: Public Archaeology
nodes.description: The engagement of archaeology with public audiences and heritage.

nodes.name: Archaeology of the Americas
nodes.description: The archaeology of the Indigenous societies of North and South America.

nodes.name: Archaeology of China
nodes.description: The archaeology of China from the Paleolithic to the dynastic era.

nodes.name: Archaeology of South Asia
nodes.description: The archaeology of the Indian subcontinent, including the Indus civilization.

nodes.name: Culture-Historical Archaeology
nodes.description: The approach that traces past peoples through the distribution of distinctive cultures.

nodes.name: Processual Archaeology
nodes.description: The mid-century approach explaining cultural change through adaptive systems.

nodes.name: Post-Processual Archaeology
nodes.description: The interpretive approach emphasizing meaning, agency, and subjectivity.

nodes.name: Excavation
nodes.description: The systematic digging and recording of archaeological deposits.

nodes.name: Archaeological Survey
nodes.description: The systematic search for and mapping of sites across a landscape.

nodes.name: Stratigraphy
nodes.description: The study of layered deposits to establish the sequence of occupation.

nodes.name: Archaeological Dating
nodes.description: The techniques for establishing the age of sites and artifacts.

nodes.name: Remote Sensing Archaeology
nodes.description: The detection of buried sites through aerial and geophysical survey.

nodes.name: Artifact Analysis
nodes.description: The classification and study of recovered objects and their manufacture.

nodes.name: Radiocarbon Dating
nodes.description: The dating of organic remains by the decay of carbon-14.

nodes.name: Dendrochronology
nodes.description: The dating of wood by matching tree-ring patterns.

nodes.name: Paleolithic Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of hunter-gatherer societies of the Old Stone Age.

nodes.name: Neolithic Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of the first farming and settled societies.

nodes.name: Bronze Age Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of the first metallurgical and state societies.

nodes.name: Greek Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of the Greek world from the Bronze Age to the Hellenistic era.

nodes.name: Roman Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of Rome and its empire.

nodes.name: Osteoarchaeology
nodes.description: The study of human skeletal remains from archaeological contexts.

nodes.name: Paleopathology
nodes.description: The study of disease and trauma in ancient human remains.

nodes.name: Community Archaeology
nodes.description: Archaeology conducted with and for descendant and local communities.

nodes.name: Mesoamerican Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of the Maya, Aztec, and earlier Mesoamerican societies.

nodes.name: Andean Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of the Andes, including the Inca and earlier cultures.

nodes.name: North American Archaeology
nodes.description: The archaeology of Indigenous societies north of Mexico.
